_comment: Migration Validator — PostgreSQL→Snowflake Transformation Rules Catalog v3.0. Single source of truth for ALL normalization rules. Aligned to the project specification: Boolean→'1'/'0', Numeric rounded to 2dp, Timestamps formatted YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS (microseconds stripped), UUID uppercased, Text trimmed, NULL→'<<NULL>>', Snowflake side adds WHERE _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE=TRUE.

rules.description: PostgreSQL BOOLEAN (true/false) and Snowflake BOOLEAN (TRUE/FALSE) are both normalised to text '1' (true) or '0' (false). NULL → '<<NULL>>' via COALESCE wrapper. This avoids case differences (true vs TRUE) and ensures direct text comparison.
rules.pg_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = true THEN '1' WHEN {col} = false THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.sf_expression: CASE WHEN {col} = TRUE THEN '1' WHEN {col} = FALSE THEN '0' ELSE NULL END
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts TRUE/FALSE to text 1 or 0. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.' Using '1'/'0' (not 'TRUE'/'FALSE') eliminates all case differences.

rules.description: Rounds numeric/decimal values to 2 decimal places (agreed precision) then converts to text. Prevents false mismatches caused by floating-point precision differences introduced by Fivetran or ETL tools. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Rounds values to 2 decimal places (or the agreed precision), then converts to text.' Default precision is 2dp — override per column if required.

rules.description: Formats TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'. Strips fractional seconds (microseconds) so precision differences between PostgreSQL (6 decimal places) and Snowflake TIMESTAMP_NTZ do not create false mismatches. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Formats as YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS, removing fractional seconds so microsecond differences do not create false mismatches.'

rules.description: Converts timezone-aware timestamps to UTC then formats as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'. Eliminates timezone offset differences that may have been introduced during ETL migration. Strips fractional seconds. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts to a common timestamp format (or UTC if required), then formats as YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS.'

rules.description: Formats DATE columns as 'YYYY-MM-DD' text for uniform comparison. DATE is consistent between PostgreSQL and Snowflake but must be converted to text for equality comparison. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Formats as YYYY-MM-DD. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from text/varchar/char columns. Empty string '' remains as '' — NOT converted to NULL (kept semantically different from NULL). NULL → '<<NULL>>'. This is also the DEFAULT FALLBACK for unrecognised type pairs.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Trims leading and trailing spaces. Empty string remains blank (kept different from NULL). If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Converts UUID to UPPERCASE text and trims spaces. PostgreSQL stores UUID natively in lowercase (xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx); Snowflake stores as VARCHAR which Fivetran may load in UPPERCASE. Uppercasing both eliminates case differences. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts to uppercase text and trims spaces. Converted to uppercase and trimmed before comparison. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Casts integer-family columns to text for cross-system comparison. PostgreSQL INTEGER is 32-bit, BIGINT is 64-bit; Snowflake NUMBER is arbitrary precision. Converting both to text string representation eliminates type-width mismatches. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts to text. Converted to text. If NULL shows <<NULL>>.'

rules.description: Converts JSON into a canonical text representation before comparison. PostgreSQL JSONB::text serialises with sorted keys and normalised whitespace. Snowflake TO_JSON(PARSE_JSON(...)) produces a canonical form. Eliminates key-ordering and formatting differences. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts JSON into a canonical text representation before comparison.' JSONB in PostgreSQL automatically sorts keys alphabetically, enabling consistent comparison.

rules.display_name: HStore → CAST to TEXT then TRIM
rules.description: Casts PostgreSQL hstore (key-value store) to TEXT before trimming. Fivetran converts hstore to JSON-like text in Snowflake (VARCHAR/TEXT). The CAST to TEXT must occur BEFORE TRIM because PostgreSQL TRIM() does not accept hstore type directly. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: PostgreSQL hstore type requires explicit CAST to TEXT before any string function (TRIM, LENGTH, etc.) can be applied. Fivetran migrates hstore as JSON-formatted text string.

rules.description: Converts binary data into a hexadecimal text representation before comparison. PostgreSQL encode(col,'hex') produces lowercase hex; Snowflake LOWER(HEX_ENCODE(col)) normalised to lowercase for consistency. NULL → '<<NULL>>'.
rules.notes: Project spec: 'Converts binary data into a hexadecimal/text representation before comparison.' Both sides normalised to lowercase hex for consistent comparison.

null_rule.description: Universal NULL handling applied to ALL columns. SQL NULL ≠ NULL (NULL comparisons always return NULL/unknown). Converting NULL to '<<NULL>>' sentinel makes comparisons work correctly. Applied as the outermost COALESCE wrapper after all other transformations.
null_rule.notes: Project spec: '<<NULL>> placeholder → SQL treats NULL ≠ NULL; converting NULL to a comparable value avoids false mismatches.' Applied to EVERY column regardless of type.

fivetran_filter.description: Snowflake-side filter added when _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE column is detected. Ensures only the LATEST active record is compared instead of historical Fivetran change-tracking snapshots.
fivetran_filter.notes: Project spec: 'WHERE _FIVETRAN_ACTIVE = TRUE — ensures only the latest active record is compared instead of historical snapshots.' Auto-detected by SnowflakeExtractor.has_fivetran_active().

rule_application_order.description: Rules applied innermost to outermost — type-specific transformation first, NULL placeholder last.
order: integer   (CAST to text — innermost for integer types)
